topic: Remaining build-cycle levers: nextest + slow-test quarantine, RUSTY_V8_ARCHIVE, root-crate splits
notes:
Peeled from thread-36f3cced after the two dominant levers landed (env-unify b5069cc: sccache reaches all dispatched shells; target-seed a0f03fc: CoW worktree seeding — cold 25-40min builds → ~45s clone+incremental, live-verified through the cockpit). Remaining, in value order:

1. NEXTEST + SLOW-TEST QUARANTINE: the full-lib gate is ~610s of EXECUTION (it outgrew the 600s brief budget mid-w11; briefs now say 900s). cargo-nextest typically 2-3x wall on suites this shape + per-test timeouts that would have named the slow index/search test instead of silently clipping. Quarantine the known 60s+ tests (search/index agentic test, system_events 10k-compaction) behind a `slow` pass run at fold-time only; per-cycle gate target <3min. Touches the campaign validation-gate convention (full lib at every fold) — keep the FULL gate at fold, shrink the mid-cycle one.

2. RUSTY_V8_ARCHIVE shared cache: rusty_v8's prebuilt archive lands in per-target OUT_DIR — re-fetched/extracted per cold worktree. Likely SUBSUMED by seed_dirs (the seeded target carries it); verify with one cold-vs-seeded build log diff before doing anything, close as no-op if subsumed.

3. ROOT-CRATE SPLITS (structural, design-work-per-cut): root blackbox crate is 168.7k LOC / 273 files (corrected from gap-fe4dd97f's stale 277k/422 — ~110k already extracted incl. bbox-refactor 91.6k). Remaining value: smaller serial tail + cheaper relink on daemon edits. Clean seams: index/, workflow/; orchestration/ is the state-coupled hard one. Wants the gap-fe4dd97f extract_rust_crate facility first (workspace scaffolder + crate-aware path rewrite + DAG guard) rather than hand-cutting.

Item 2 (RUSTY_V8_ARCHIVE shared cache) VERIFIED SUBSUMED by seed_dirs — closing as no-op. Live cold-vs-seeded diff (2026-06-10, throwaway worktrees, `cargo check -p v8 -vv`):

- The 139MB prebuilt archive lives at `target/<profile>/gn_out/obj/librusty_v8.a` + `.sum` (URL receipt) — INSIDE target/, so the CoW seed carries it (verified: identical mtime in clone).
- Seeded worktree: v8 build script DOES re-run (worktree path changes cargo's unit hash — fingerprints don't transfer for v8's build unit), but build.rs checks the .sum receipt against the expected URL and SKIPS the download. 6.2s total, zero network, archive untouched.
- Cold worktree: real re-download per worktree ("Downloading ... Done", ~9s total on this host/network). rusty_v8 checks a user-global cache at ~/.cargo/.rusty_v8/ first but never WRITES it, so it stays empty — no help.
- No action: every dispatch path that creates worktrees (cockpit + workflow WorktreeCreate) seeds target/, so the cold path only occurs on seed failure (non-CoW volume), where the marginal cost is ~seconds on this network. RUSTY_V8_ARCHIVE env pinning not worth the config surface.

Remaining items: 1 (nextest + slow-test quarantine — next up, the substantive win) and 3 (root-crate splits — parked on gap-fe4dd97f extract_rust_crate facility).

Item 1 (nextest + slow-test quarantine) IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-10). cargo-nextest 0.9.137 installed via brew. Baseline `cargo nextest run --lib` (no config): 1870 tests / 1870 pass / 79.95s wall — process-per-test parallelism alone is ~7.6x vs the ~610s cargo test gate. Exactly two tests pin the tail: index::search::agentic_project_file_tests::registered_project_markdown_and_rust_source_are_searchable (78.6s) and system_events::store::tests::compact_caps_at_ten_thousand_keeping_newest (55.2s); next-slowest 5.2s.

Shipped `.config/nextest.toml`: profile `default` (mid-cycle gate) quarantines those two via default-filter + slow-timeout {30s, terminate-after 4} so newly slow tests get NAMED, not silently absorbed; profile `full` (fold/closeout gate) runs all() with {60s, terminate-after 5}. Verified: default gate 1868 pass / 16.2s wall (610s → 16s, far under the <3min target); full gate 1870 pass / 81.8s, 78s test flagged SLOW not killed; `nextest list` confirms quarantined pair excluded from default, present in full.

Process-per-test note: test_env_lock() in-process mutex no longer serializes under nextest but per-process env isolation supersedes it (all-green run is the empirical proof); lock still required for plain cargo test. Docs updated: PROJECT.md Validation (nextest as baseline, full profile at fold, cargo test fallback), docs/developing-blackbox.md Build-and-test, CHANGELOG Unreleased. Uncommitted in working tree. Remaining in thread: item 3 only (root-crate splits, parked on gap-fe4dd97f extract_rust_crate).

Item 3 topology RE-MEASURED (2026-06-10) — original note's plan is half-stale. Sizes hold: root 169.4k LOC / 273 files (note said 168.7k/273); 7 bbox-* leaf crates extracted ~119k (bbox-refactor 91.6k, bbox-macros 15k, rest small).

STALE: "clean seams: index/, workflow/". Measured coupling says otherwise — index/ has 14 distinct internal deps (projects, transcripts, knowledge, parser, entity_ref...) and is imported by 19 outside files; workflow/ has 13 incl. 8x use crate::server + 8x use crate::orchestration. Both are mid-graph; cutting them is dependency-inversion design work, not a peel.

CORRECTED plan: (a) next mechanical peel is packets/ — 7.1k LOC, ZERO external internal deps, true leaf, same extract+re-export pattern as the prior bbox-* cuts; (b) small leaves behind it: council/ (2.5k, 2 deps), system_memory/ (1.2k, 2), embed/ (2.9k, 4), transcripts/ (2.7k, 4), providers/ (2.4k, 5) — leaf-peeling ceiling ≈ root 169k → ~150k, modest; (c) the REAL serial tail is the tools/ (29.9k, 39 deps) + server/ (11.1k, 28) + orchestration/ (28.9k, imported by 45 files — most-depended-upon big module) + workflow/ (13.5k) interlock, ~83k LOC of top-of-graph integration — needs design-level decoupling, extract_rust_crate scaffolder (gap-fe4dd97f) alone won't unlock it. orchestration-is-hard intuition confirmed but for the inverse reason: low fan-out (8), massive fan-in (45).

Item 3 first cut SHIPPED (2026-06-10, commit a0217f5): packets/ peeled into crates/bbox-packets, solo in an isolated worktree (no fan-out — single serial chain, contention on Cargo.toml/lib.rs). Root crate 169.4k → ~162k LOC, 273 → 259 files.

Decoupling that made it a true leaf: (1) json_store → bbox-corpus-core (dep-free 133-line helper, root alias keeps 13 call sites unchanged); (2) util::now_iso → bbox-corpus-core::util (root re-export); (3) companion gap-note INGESTION inverted root-side as gaps::emit_companion_packet_gap_note — packets keeps body composition (gap_dedupe_key/build_gap_note_body), gaps.rs owns GapStore writes; 5 companion-gap integration tests moved to gaps::packet_companion_tests so they stay in the root gate. rmcp dep kept (schemars re-export, matches bbox-refactor/bbox-macros precedent). corpus-core Cargo.toml comment had already reserved this growth ("util/json_store ... as later stages need them").

Validation: cargo check clean, root --lib gate 1768 pass/15.9s, bbox-packets+corpus-core 128 pass, clippy 0 warnings root+leaves, lint-concurrency ok.

OPEN DECISION surfaced while peeling: the documented `cargo nextest run --lib` gate covers the ROOT PACKAGE ONLY — bbox-refactor's 854 in-crate tests were already outside it, and bbox-packets' 105 now join them. Options: adopt --workspace in the gate docs (needs a timing + green-ness measurement across bro-harness etc.) or accept per-crate -p runs as targeted recipes. Operator decision pending.

Remaining in item 3: small leaves (council 2.5k, system_memory 1.2k, embed 2.9k, transcripts 2.7k, providers 2.4k @ 2-5 deps each), then the hard ~83k tools/server/orchestration/workflow interlock (design-level decoupling).

Gate-scope decision RESOLVED (commit a83b841): gates are now WORKSPACE-WIDE. Measurements (warm target, 14 threads): workspace --lib 3,522 pass / 21.5s; workspace all-targets 3,700 pass / 23.8s; workspace full profile 3,702 pass / 84.8s (pinned by the 80s index test). The root-only gate had been silently excluding ~1,800 tests (854 bbox-refactor, 105 bbox-packets, bro-* crates, 57 bro-slack bin tests, integration tests). Full coverage costs only +8s over root-only, so --workspace becomes the documented default in nextest.toml header, PROJECT.md, developing-blackbox.md, and knowledge entry df711bd7 (updated + re-rendered). No executable doctests exist (all fences are ignore/json), so nextest's no-doctest gap costs nothing. bro-lsp's rust-analyzer integration test self-skips when RA is absent — gate-safe on any host.

Build story measured + documented in developing-blackbox.md: no-op check 0.2s, root-edit check 3.3s, leaf-edit check 3.5s, blackboxd binary rebuild after root edit ~31s (codegen+link), legacy cargo test --lib ~610s. One spurious LEAK observed once on orchestration::atoms::registry::tests::parse_rejects_empty (one-line assert; not reproducible in 3 re-runs; fd-attribution noise, not chased).

Thread state: items 1+2 done, gate story done. Item 3 continues: next peels council/system_memory/embed/transcripts/providers (2-5 deps each), then the ~83k tools/server/orchestration/workflow interlock (design-level).

Small-leaf round SHIPPED (commit 3f93525): bbox-system-memory new leaf crate (1.2k); query.rs (214), template.rs (71, tera), search/ rrf+rerank (222) folded into bbox-corpus-core. Root crate now 160.9k LOC / 250 files (from 169.4k/273 pre-packets). Workspace gate 3,714 pass / 24.3s, clippy 0, lint-concurrency ok.

New reusable pattern learned: cross-crate cfg(test) inversion — a peeled module's #[cfg(test)] pub helpers are configured OUT when the crate compiles as a dependency of the consumer's test build, and env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) silently re-roots to the crate subdir. Fix shape: leaf exposes un-gated *_from(&dir) test-support fn; consumer owns repo-root fixture paths in its own cfg(test) helper (util::init_system_memory_for_tests, 7 call sites); leaf-internal fixture tests use ../../ manifest-relative paths.

SMALL-LEAF LANE NOW EXHAUSTED. Inline-ref measurement (not use-statement counts) disqualified the rest: council (orchestration allocator/dispatch_prelude/team + server state — it IS orchestration), embed (index ×12, artifacts ×9, orchestration ×5), transcripts (index schema machinery ×9; its ONLY orchestration coupling is the Provider enum — flag for a contract-bottom move when the interlock work starts), providers (system_memory ×4 now via crate, orchestration, artifacts, edge_index), code_nav residue (index ×9). What remains of item 3 is the ~83k tools/server/orchestration/workflow interlock — design-level decoupling (candidate first move: Provider enum down to a contract crate), plus the gap-fe4dd97f extract_rust_crate facility for mechanizing future cuts.

gap-fe4dd97f RESOLVED (commit c8ff47f): extract_rust_crate facility shipped in bbox-refactor. Item 3's mechanization dependency is now in place — future leaf peels are one bbox_refactor_run step (scaffold + DAG guard + cargo check --workspace + compile-fix + rollback) instead of a hand-performed sequence. v1 contract: re-export-alias shape (no mass path rewrite), fail-closed leaf invariant (refuses non-leaf modules listing crate::<other> offenders file:line — the same coupling scan this thread ran manually for the candidate survey). rewrite_rust_crate_paths (with use-tree splitting) exists for future alias-free cleanup; rust_workspace_dag_check is a reusable standalone guard. Side fix: analysis-only kinds now legal as run steps. What remains of item 3 is unchanged: the ~83k tools/server/orchestration/workflow interlock needs design-level decoupling (first candidate: Provider enum → contract bottom) before this facility can cut it.

Provider-enum move executed (commit 4e15de3) — and the finding is better than expected: the TYPE move had already happened (bro-core owns the pure Provider identity; orchestration/providers.rs re-exports it + owns the ProviderExec/Events/Mcp/Session dispatch traits). What remained was import-path hygiene: corpus-side consumers routed through crate::orchestration::providers::, keeping a phantom module edge. Swapped 11 pure-identity uses to bro_core::Provider (same type, zero behavior change): transcripts/ ×5 (its ONLY orchestration coupling) and index/ ×6 (helpers.rs harness-provider list + reindex test).

New topology: transcripts/ depends on exactly ONE root module (index ×9; parser/entity_ref already crate aliases); index/ has ZERO orchestration refs. The future index-cluster extraction (index + transcripts together, likely + code_nav residue) no longer drags orchestration — it's now bounded by index/'s remaining root deps (knowledge, projects, threads, roadmap, edge_index, store_persister, query→corpus-core already, git→corpus-core already...). Next decoupling candidates for that cluster, in the same lens: what does index/ reference per-family and which of those are themselves peelable or invertible. embed/ (AgentManifest types) and providers/ (brofile/task plumbing) keep REAL orchestration coupling — different work. Gate: 3,721 pass. Gap record close-out committed (2dfe834).
